title: Voyager Trajectory
definition: The path of Voyager 1 as it moves through space, including its direction and angle of departure from the solar system.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine a tiny spaceship leaving Earth and its path through space. It doesn't just go straight out, but also banks up at a 35° angle, like taking off from a runway.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Voyager 1's trajectory is a combination of two main movements: it travels outward from the solar system at a 35° angle relative to the galactic plane, and it does so after using gravitational slingshots around Jupiter and Saturn to increase its speed.
difficulty_levels.expert: The Voyager trajectory is a fascinating example of the gravitational slingshot effect in action. By using these slingshots, Voyager 1 was able to leave the solar system with a velocity of 17 kilometers per second, which is approximately 60,000 kilometers per hour. This trajectory allows us to explore the outer edges of the solar system and the interstellar medium.

extra_fields.insight: The Voyager trajectory is a unique visual representation of the gravitational slingshot effect, demonstrating the combination of outward and upward movement required to leave the solar system.
